Summary and sentiment (adjusted using Beige Book insights):
- Policy signal: The FOMC delivered a modestly dovish 25 bp cut to 4.5–4.75% with balanced-risk guidance while continuing QT. This supports debt service and should aid activity over time as inflation continues to move toward target.
- Beige Book check: District reports indicate slight-to-modest growth, softer/mixed consumer spending, and easing labor market conditions with moderating wage pressures. Price increases slowed further but remain somewhat elevated in select categories. Credit conditions stayed tight: small businesses faced tighter C&I standards and weaker loan demand; CRE remained weak (especially office) with only limited easing for multifamily at large banks; household credit tightened for subprime while prime RRE/HELOC standards were largely unchanged. These details align with the October SLOOS, reinforcing a still-restrictive bank credit channel.
- Net: The rate cut and ongoing disinflation are positives, but Beige Book/SLOOS headwinds—particularly for small firms and CRE—temper the near-term impulse. Tone is slightly positive but more restrained than a pure “dovish” read.
